purpose: Query-conditioned retrieval from reconstructed state with explicit query anchors and dependency closure.
caveats: This is selective state transfer, not end-to-end retrieval/index discovery: query anchors and dependency selection are supplied deterministically from the original query specification and their discovery/index cost is excluded from transported state cost.
multi_hop_recall_pct measures dependency-closure completeness, not learned retriever recall.
Conditioned token reduction is measured against full encoded memory plus the same explicit query payload; it does not claim a global minimum or optimal representation.
Evidence is deterministic representation/state utility only; it does not establish LLM semantic equivalence, latency, universal generalization, or consciousness.
interpretation: Across 450 deterministic cases, all three representations reconstructed exact state and produced exact answers after query-conditioned dependency transfer. The conditioned payload contained about 0.792% of the full state count on average, while preserving exact answers. Mean input-token reduction was 99.12% for Sim17 compact, 99.03% for structural-lineage, and 99.02% for state-columnar under cl100k_base. This is evidence that once query anchors are explicit, the required structural dependency closure can be transported at a much smaller payload than the full compressed memory in this benchmark; it is not evidence that an autonomous retriever can discover that closure without an index or query metadata.
